neighbours.label: the likelihood idiom: ' chance' in 'there's a (good) chance' and ' are' in 'chances are / odds are'
fire: If you leave early, there's a good chance you'll miss the traffic.
He studied hard, so chances are he passed the exam.
Look in the garage; odds are the ladder is still there.
Bring a coat, because there's a chance it will rain during the parade.
If you bought it last year, chances are the warranty still covers it.
We left late, and odds are the store will be closed when we arrive.
The airline warned that there's a small chance the flight gets delayed again.
With that many cooks, chances are the soup is too salty.
quiet: If you leave early, you'll probably miss the traffic.
He studied hard, so he probably passed the exam.
Look in the garage; the ladder is likely still there.
Bring a coat, because it will probably rain during the parade.
If you bought it last year, the warranty may still cover it.
We left late, and the store will probably be closed when we arrive.
The airline warned that the flight might get delayed again.
With that many cooks, the soup is probably too salty.

notes: Near misses keep the hedged meaning with probably/likely/might and drop chance/odds.
